types.name: AgentActivity
types.description: An activity performed by or directed at an AI coding agent during a session. Activities represent the observable steps of an agent's work, including thoughts, actions (tool calls), responses, prompts from users, errors, and elicitation requests. Each activity belongs to an agent session and is associated with the user who initiated it.

fields.name: queued
fields.description: [Internal] Whether this activity is queued for later processing. Queued activities are not sent to the agent until the session reaches a terminal state.

types.name: AgentActivityPushSummary
types.description: [Internal] What a coding agent turn pushed to its branch, measured in the sandbox at push time. The range is cumulative within a turn, so a turn that pushes several times reports every commit each time — consumers use the last summary in a turn rather than combining across pushes.

fields.description: Shas of the turn's commits beyond the detailed cap, newest first. Stats aren't captured for these.

fields.description: The commit the turn started from — the sandbox HEAD when the prompt began.

fields.description: The number of non-merge commits the turn added. Equals the length of commits plus additionalCommitShas.

fields.name: commits
fields.description: The turn's non-merge commits with stats, newest first. Capped, so it may hold fewer commits than commitCount reports.

fields.name: headSha
fields.description: The commit that was pushed.

types.name: AgentSession
types.description: A session representing an AI coding agent's work on an issue or conversation. Agent sessions track the lifecycle of an agent's engagement, from creation through active work to completion or dismissal. Each session is associated with an agent user (the bot), optionally a human creator, an issue, and a comment thread where the agent posts updates. Sessions contain activities that record the agent's observable steps and can be linked to pull requests created during the work.

fields.description: Activities associated with this agent session.

types.name: Customer
types.description: A customer organization tracked in Linear's customer management system. Customers represent external companies or organizations whose product requests and feedback are captured as customer needs, which can be linked to issues and projects. Customers can be associated with domains, external system IDs, Slack channels, and managed by integrations such as Intercom or Salesforce.

fields.name: approximateNeedCount
fields.description: The approximate count of customer needs (requests) associated with this customer. This is a denormalized counter and may not reflect the exact count at all times.

fields.name: archivedAt
fields.description: The time at which the entity was archived. Null if the entity has not been archived.

fields.name: createdAt
fields.description: The time at which the entity was created.

fields.name: domains
fields.description: The email domains associated with this customer (e.g., 'acme.com'). Used to automatically match incoming requests to this customer. Public email domains (e.g., gmail.com) are not allowed. Domains must be unique across all customers in the workspace.

fields.name: externalIds
fields.description: Identifiers for this customer in external systems (e.g., CRM IDs from Intercom, Salesforce, or HubSpot). Used for matching customers during integration syncs and upsert operations. External IDs must be unique across customers in the workspace.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The unique identifier of the entity.

fields.name: integration
fields.description: The integration that manages this customer's data (e.g., Intercom, Salesforce). Null if the customer is not managed by any data source integration.

fields.name: logoUrl
fields.description: URL of the customer's logo image. Null if no logo has been uploaded.

fields.name: mainSourceId
fields.description: The primary external source ID when a customer has data from multiple external systems. Must be one of the values in the externalIds array. Null if the customer has zero or one external source.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The display name of the customer organization.

fields.name: needs
fields.description: The list of customer needs (product requests and feedback) associated with this customer.

fields.name: owner
fields.description: The workspace member assigned as the owner of this customer. Null if no owner has been assigned. App users cannot be set as customer owners.

fields.name: revenue
fields.description: The annual revenue generated by this customer. Null if revenue data has not been provided. May be synced from an external data source such as a CRM integration.

fields.name: size
fields.description: The number of employees or seats at the customer organization. Null if size data has not been provided. May be synced from an external data source such as a CRM integration.

fields.name: slackChannelId
fields.description: The ID of the Slack channel linked to this customer for communication. Null if no Slack channel has been associated. Must be unique across all customers in the workspace.

fields.name: slugId
fields.description: A unique, human-readable URL slug for the customer. Automatically generated and used in customer page URLs.

fields.name: status
fields.description: The current lifecycle status of the customer. Defaults to the first status by position when a customer is created without an explicit status.

fields.name: tier
fields.description: The tier or segment assigned to this customer for prioritization (e.g., Enterprise, Pro, Free). Null if no tier has been assigned.

fields.name: updatedAt
fields.description:
The last time at which the entity was meaningfully updated. This is the same as the creation time if the entity hasn't
    been updated after creation.

fields.name: url
fields.description: The URL of the customer's page in the Linear application.

types.name: CustomerNeed
types.description: A customer need represents a specific product request or piece of feedback from a customer. Customer needs serve as the bridge between customer feedback and engineering work by linking a customer to an issue or project, optionally with a comment or attachment providing additional context. Needs can be created manually, from integrations, or from intake sources like email.

fields.name: archivedAt
fields.description: The time at which the entity was archived. Null if the entity has not been archived.

fields.name: attachment
fields.description: The issue attachment linked to this need. Populated when the need originates from an intake source (e.g., Slack, Intercom) or when a URL is manually provided. Provides a link back to the original source of the customer feedback. Mutually exclusive with projectAttachment.

fields.name: body
fields.description: The body content of the need in Markdown format. Used to capture manual input about needs that cannot be directly tied to an attachment. Null if the need's content comes from an attached source.

fields.name: bodyData
fields.description: [Internal] The body content of the need as a Prosemirror document JSON string. This is the structured representation of the body field, used for rich text rendering in the editor.

fields.name: comment
fields.description: An optional comment providing additional context for this need. Null if the need was not created from or associated with a specific comment.

fields.name: content
fields.description: The effective Markdown content shown for this customer need. Returns the manually stored body when present, otherwise falls back to content extracted from the source attachment. Null if no content is available.

fields.name: createdAt
fields.description: The time at which the entity was created.

fields.name: creator
fields.description: The user who manually created this customer need. Null for needs created automatically by integrations or intake sources.

fields.name: customer
fields.description: The customer organization this need belongs to. Null if the need has not yet been associated with a customer.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The unique identifier of the entity.

fields.name: issue
fields.description: The issue this need is linked to. Either issueId or projectId must be set. When set, the need's projectId is denormalized from the issue's project.

fields.name: originalIssue
fields.description: The issue this customer need was originally created on, before being moved to a different issue or project. Null if the customer need has not been moved from its original location.

fields.name: priority
fields.description: Whether the customer need is important or not. 0 = Not important, 1 = Important.

fields.name: project
fields.description: The project this need is linked to. For issue-based needs, this is denormalized from the issue's project. For project-only needs, this is set directly.

fields.name: projectAttachment
fields.description: The project attachment linked to this need. Populated when the need originates from an intake source or when a URL is manually provided for a project-level need. Provides a link back to the original source of the customer feedback. Mutually exclusive with attachment.

fields.name: updatedAt
fields.description:
The last time at which the entity was meaningfully updated. This is the same as the creation time if the entity hasn't
    been updated after creation.

fields.name: url
fields.description: The URL of the source attachment linked to this need, if any. Returns the URL from either the issue attachment or project attachment. Null if the need has no attached source.

types.name: Cycle
types.description: A time-boxed iteration (similar to a sprint) used for planning and tracking work. Cycles belong to a team and have defined start and end dates. Issues are assigned to cycles for time-based planning, and progress is tracked via completed, in-progress, and total scope. Cycles are automatically completed when their end date passes, and uncompleted issues can be carried over to the next cycle.

types.name: Issue
types.description: An issue is the core work item in Linear. Issues belong to a team, have a workflow status, can be assigned to users, carry a priority level, and can be organized into projects and cycles. Issues support sub-issues (parent-child hierarchy up to 10 levels deep), labels, due dates, estimates, and SLA tracking. They can also be linked to other issues via relations, attached to releases, and tracked through their full history of changes.

types.name: IssueDraft
types.description: [Internal] A draft issue that has not yet been created as a full issue. Drafts allow users to prepare issue details (title, description, labels, assignee, etc.) before committing them. Drafts belong to a team and a creator, and support a parent-child hierarchy similar to issues. A draft can have either a parent draft or a parent issue, but not both.

fields.description: The time at which the entity was archived. Null if the entity has not been archived.

fields.name: assigneeId

fields.name: delegateId
fields.description: The agent user delegated to work on the issue being drafted.

fields.name: description
fields.description: The draft's description in markdown format.

fields.name: descriptionData
fields.description: [Internal] The draft's description as a Prosemirror document.

fields.name: dueDate

fields.name: id

fields.name: labelIds

types.name: NotificationSubscription

types.name: OauthClientApproval
types.description: A request to install an OAuth client application on a workspace, along with the admin's approval or denial response. When a user attempts to install an OAuth application that requires admin approval, an approval record is created. A workspace admin can then approve or deny the request, optionally providing a reason. The record also tracks any newly requested scopes that were added after the initial approval.

fields.description: The time at which the entity was created.

fields.description: An optional explanation from the admin for why the installation request was denied.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The unique identifier of the entity.

fields.name: newlyRequestedScopes
fields.description: Additional OAuth scopes requested after the initial approval. These scopes are not yet approved and require a separate admin decision. Null if no additional scopes have been requested. These scopes will never overlap with the already-approved scopes.

fields.description: The identifier of the user who initiated the request to install the OAuth client application.

fields.name: responderId
fields.description: The identifier of the workspace admin who approved or denied the installation request. Null if the request has not yet been responded to.

fields.name: scopes
fields.description: The OAuth scopes that the application has been approved to use within this workspace (e.g., 'read', 'write', 'issues:create').

fields.name: status
fields.description: The current status of the approval request: requested (pending admin review), approved, or denied.

fields.description:

types.name: PullRequest
types.description: [Internal] A pull or merge request from a connected version control system (GitHub or GitLab). Pull requests are automatically linked to Linear issues via branch names or commit messages containing issue identifiers. They track the full lifecycle including status, reviewers, checks, and merge state, and are synced bidirectionally with the hosting provider.

fields.name: archivedAt
fields.description: The time at which the entity was archived. Null if the entity has not been archived.

fields.name: autoMergeEnabled
fields.description: Whether auto-merge is enabled for the pull request.

fields.name: baseSha
fields.description: The Git SHA of the base commit on the target branch that the pull request is compared against. Null if not yet synced.

fields.name: checks
fields.description: [Internal] The CI/CD checks and status checks associated with the pull request, synced from the hosting provider.

fields.name: closedAt
fields.description: The time at which the pull request was closed. Hosting providers also set this when a pull request is merged, so read `status` to tell a closed pull request from a merged one. Null while the pull request is still open.

fields.name: commits
fields.description: [ALPHA] The commits included in the pull request, synced from the hosting provider. Includes metadata such as SHA, message, diff stats, and author information.

fields.name: createdAt
fields.description: The time at which the entity was created.

fields.name: creator
fields.description: [Internal] The Linear user who created the pull request. Null if the creator is an external user not mapped to a Linear account, or if the creator's account has been deleted.

fields.name: hasConflicts
fields.description: Whether the source branch has conflicts with the target branch. When true, the conflicts must be resolved before the pull request can be merged. This is reported separately from `mergeStatus`, which describes whether the pull request is blocked by required approvals or checks.

fields.name: headSha
fields.description: The Git SHA of the latest commit on the source branch. Updated as new commits are pushed. Null if not yet synced.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The unique identifier of the entity.

fields.name: isBehind
fields.description: Whether the source branch is behind the target branch. When true, the source branch is missing commits that have landed on the target branch since it was last updated.

fields.name: mergeCommit
fields.description: The merge commit created when the pull request was merged. Null if the pull request has not been merged or if the merge commit data is not available.

fields.name: mergeSettings
fields.description: Merge settings and allowed merge methods for this pull request's repository. Null if the settings have not been synced from the provider.

fields.name: mergeStatus
fields.description: The current merge status of the pull request, synced from the hosting provider.

fields.name: mergedAt
fields.description: The time at which the pull request was merged. Null if the pull request has not been merged.

fields.name: nativeStackId
fields.description: [Internal] The host-qualified external ID of the native stack that contains this pull request. Null if the pull request is not in a native stack or stack data is unavailable.

fields.name: nativeStackNumber
fields.description: [Internal] The number the hosting provider assigns to the native stack within its repository. Null if the pull request is not in a native stack or stack data is unavailable.

fields.name: nativeStackPosition
fields.description: [Internal] The pull request's one-based position in its native stack, where 1 is closest to the target branch. Null if the pull request is not in a native stack or stack data is unavailable.

fields.name: nativeStackSize
fields.description: [Internal] The total number of pull requests in the native stack. Null if the pull request is not in a native stack or stack data is unavailable.

fields.name: nativeStackTargetBranch
fields.description: [Internal] The target branch shared by the native stack. Null if the pull request is not in a native stack or stack data is unavailable.

fields.name: number
fields.description: The pull request number as assigned by the hosting provider (e.g., #123 on GitHub). Unique within a repository.

fields.name: openedAt
fields.description: The time at which the pull request was opened.

fields.name: previewLinks
fields.description: [Internal] The deploy/build preview links parsed from the pull request description and comments.

fields.name: reactionData
fields.description: Emoji reaction summary for this pull request, grouped by emoji type. Each entry contains the emoji name, count, and the IDs of users who reacted.

fields.name: reactions
fields.description: Reactions associated with this pull request.

fields.name: slugId
fields.description: The pull request's unique URL slug, used to construct human-readable URLs within the Linear app.

fields.name: sourceBranch
fields.description: The source (head) branch of the pull request that contains the proposed changes.

fields.name: status
fields.description: The current status of the pull request (open, closed, merged, or draft). Synced from the hosting provider.

fields.name: targetBranch
fields.description: The target (base) branch that the pull request will be merged into.

fields.name: title
fields.description: The title of the pull request.

fields.name: updatedAt
fields.description:
The last time at which the entity was meaningfully updated. This is the same as the creation time if the entity hasn't
    been updated after creation.

fields.name: url
fields.description: The URL of the pull request on the hosting provider (e.g., a GitHub or GitLab URL).

types.name: PullRequestCheck
types.description: [ALPHA] A CI/CD check or status check associated with a pull request (e.g., a GitHub Actions workflow run or a required status check).

fields.name: completedAt
fields.description: The date and time when the check finished running. Null if the check has not completed yet.

fields.name: isRequired
fields.description: Whether this check is required to pass before the pull request can be merged. Null if the required status is unknown.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The name of the check.

fields.name: presentation
fields.description: How the check should be opened in the client.

fields.name: startedAt
fields.description: The date and time when the check started running. Null if the check has not started yet.

fields.name: status
fields.description: The status of the check.

fields.name: url
fields.description: The URL to view the check details on the hosting provider. Null if no URL is available.

fields.name: workflowName

types.description: An emoji reaction on a comment, issue, project update, initiative update, post, pull request, or pull request comment. Each reaction is associated with exactly one parent entity and is created by either a workspace user or an external user. Reactions are persisted individually but surfaced on their parent entities as aggregated reactionData.

fields.name: projectUpdate

The last time at which the entity was meaningfully updated. This is the same as the creation time if the entity hasn't

types.name: Release
types.description: A release that bundles issues together for a software deployment or version. Releases belong to a release pipeline and progress through stages (e.g., planned, started, completed, canceled). Issues are associated with releases via the IssueToRelease join entity, and the release tracks lifecycle timestamps such as when it was started, completed, or canceled.

fields.name: archivedAt
fields.description: The time at which the entity was archived. Null if the entity has not been archived.

fields.name: autoArchivedAt
fields.description: The time at which the release was automatically archived by the auto pruning process.

fields.name: canceledAt
fields.description: The time at which the release was canceled. Set automatically when the release moves to a canceled stage. Reset to null if the release moves back to a non-canceled stage.

fields.name: commitSha
fields.description: The Git commit SHA associated with this release. Used for SHA-based idempotency when completing releases and for linking releases to specific points in the repository history. Null if the release was created without a commit reference.

fields.name: completedAt
fields.description: The time at which the release was completed. Set automatically when the release moves to a completed stage. Reset to null if the release moves back to a non-completed stage.

fields.name: createdAt
fields.description: The time at which the entity was created.

fields.name: creator
fields.description: The user who created the release. Null if the release was created by a non-user context such as an access key or automation.

fields.name: currentProgress
fields.description: The current progress summary for the release, including counts of issues by workflow state type (e.g., completed, in progress, unstarted).

fields.name: description
fields.description: The description of the release in plain text or markdown. Null if no description has been set.

fields.name: documents
fields.description: Documents associated with the release.

types.name: SyncedExternalThread
types.description: A comment thread that is synced with an external source such as Slack, Jira, GitHub, Salesforce, or email. Provides information about the external thread's origin, its current sync status, and whether the user has the necessary personal integration connected to participate in the thread.

fields.name: displayName
fields.description: A human-readable display name for the thread, derived from the external source. For Slack threads this is the channel name, for Jira it's the issue key, for email it's the sender name and count of other participants.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The unique identifier of this synced external thread. Auto-generated if not provided.

fields.name: isConnected
fields.description: Whether this thread is currently syncing comments bidirectionally with the external service. False if the external entity relation has been removed or if the thread was explicitly unsynced.

fields.name: isPersonalIntegrationConnected
fields.description: Whether the current user has a working personal integration connected for the external service. For example, whether they have connected their personal Jira, GitHub, or Slack account. A connected personal integration may still return false if it has an authentication error.

fields.name: isPersonalIntegrationRequired
fields.description: Whether a connected personal integration is required to post comments in this synced thread. True for Jira and GitHub threads, where comments must be attributed to a specific user in the external system. False for Slack and other services where the workspace integration can post on behalf of users.

fields.name: name
fields.description: A human-readable display name for the external source (e.g., 'Slack', 'Jira', 'GitHub').

fields.name: subType
fields.description: The specific integration service for the external source (e.g., 'slack', 'jira', 'github', 'salesforce'). Null if the source type does not have a sub-type.

fields.name: type
fields.description: The category of the external source (e.g., 'integration' for service integrations, 'email' for email-based threads).

fields.name: url
fields.description: A URL linking to the thread in the external service. For example, a Slack message permalink, a Jira issue URL, or a GitHub issue URL.

types.name: Team

types.name: Webhook
types.description: A webhook subscription that sends HTTP POST callbacks to an external URL when events occur in Linear. Webhooks can be scoped to a specific team, multiple teams, or all public teams in the organization. They support filtering by resource type (e.g., Issue, Comment, Project) and can be created either manually by users or automatically by OAuth applications. Each webhook has a signing secret for verifying payload authenticity on the recipient side.

types.name: __EnumValue
types.description: One possible value for a given Enum. Enum values are unique values, not a placeholder for a string or numeric value. However an Enum value is returned in a JSON response as a string.

types.name: __Field
types.description: Object and Interface types are described by a list of Fields, each of which has a name, potentially a list of arguments, and a return type.

types.name: __InputValue
types.description: Arguments provided to Fields or Directives and the input fields of an InputObject are represented as Input Values which describe their type and optionally a default value.

fields.name: defaultValue
fields.description: A GraphQL-formatted string representing the default value for this input value.

types.name: __Schema
types.description: A GraphQL Schema defines the capabilities of a GraphQL server. It exposes all available types and directives on the server, as well as the entry points for query, mutation, and subscription operations.

fields.name: types
fields.description: A list of all types supported by this server.

fields.name: queryType
fields.description: The type that query operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: mutationType
fields.description: If this server supports mutation, the type that mutation operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: subscriptionType
fields.description: If this server support subscription, the type that subscription operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: directives
fields.description: A list of all directives supported by this server.

types.name: __Type
types.description:
The fundamental unit of any GraphQL Schema is the type. There are many kinds of types in GraphQL as represented by the `__TypeKind` enum.

Depending on the kind of a type, certain fields describe information about that type. Scalar types provide no information beyond a name, description and optional `specifiedByUrl`, while Enum types provide their values. Object and Interface types provide the fields they describe. Abstract types, Union and Interface, provide the Object types possible at runtime. List and NonNull types compose other types.

types.name: __TypeKind
types.description: An enum describing what kind of type a given `__Type` is.

enumValues.name: SCALAR
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a scalar.

enumValues.name: OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an object. `fields` and `interfaces` are valid fields.

enumValues.name: INTERFACE
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an interface. `fields`, `interfaces`, and `possibleTypes` are valid fields.

enumValues.name: UNION
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a union. `possibleTypes` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: ENUM
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an enum. `enumValues` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: INPUT_OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an input object. `inputFields` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: LIST
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a list. `ofType` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: NON_NULL
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a non-null. `ofType` is a valid field.

directives.name: deprecated
directives.description: Marks an element of a GraphQL schema as no longer supported.

args.name: reason
args.description: Explains why this element was deprecated, usually also including a suggestion for how to access supported similar data. Formatted using the Markdown syntax, as specified by [CommonMark](https://commonmark.org/).

directives.name: include
directives.description: Directs the executor to include this field or fragment only when the `if` argument is true.

args.name: if
args.description: Included when true.

directives.name: oneOf
directives.description: Indicates exactly one field must be supplied and this field must not be `null`.

directives.name: skip
directives.description: Directs the executor to skip this field or fragment when the `if` argument is true.

args.name: if
args.description: Skipped when true.

directives.name: specifiedBy
directives.description: Exposes a URL that specifies the behaviour of this scalar.

args.name: url
args.description: The URL that specifies the behaviour of this scalar.
